Bra Measurement Chart

Use an international bra measurement chart to compare band and cup references across US, UK, EU, French, Australian, and Japanese sizing systems today.

International Band Reference

These are common labeling conversions, not measurements mandated for every commercial bra. ISO 8559-1 provides standardized definitions for anthropometric measurements used in clothing sizing; it does not prescribe one universal bra-size conversion table.

Frequently Asked Questions

Answers about sizing methods, measurements, and fit considerations.

How do French and Spanish band numbers compare with EU numbers? ▾

A common convention is FR/ES = EU + 15. For example, EU 70 is commonly labelled FR 85. Always confirm the product chart because labeling can vary.

What is the Australian band convention? ▾

A common Australian convention uses dress-size numbers: UK/US 28, 30, 32, 34, 36 and 38 correspond approximately to AU 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16.

Sources & Standards
